task.title: Extract unified-method descriptors from CCXT TS — TS signature + JSDoc overlay
acceptance_criteria: Mix task uses `TaskScope.parse_and_resolve!/2` for scope parsing — no direct `OptionParser.parse` call in the new mix task (per Task 144)
task.body: CCXT's unified methods carry two complementary axes: (a) the TS method signature — ordered `.value.params` with name, TS type, optional flag, default value, plus return type — the structural source of truth; (b) a leading JSDoc block adding per-param prose, `@throws {ErrorClass}` entries, `@returns` shape — the semantic overlay. Both halves matter; don't ship JSDoc alone. Extract both via an OXC pass over method definitions and emit a unified-method descriptor per method so each downstream client maps it to its own arg-shape convention — do NOT encode any single consumer's arg-shape in the descriptor. The TS-signature half is mechanical; the JSDoc half is the unknown — verify whether OXC surfaces JSDoc through `leadingComments`, a program-level comments array, or needs a second pass; QuickBEAM over the TS source is the fallback. Also emit `descriptor.source` — the byte-for-byte method body slice via OXC `.start`/`.end` offsets (provenance `raw`, just the method body, no normalization) so the descriptor becomes self-verifying. Provenance: both halves `raw`. Partial descriptors are honest (missing JSDoc → `description: null`, `errors: null` + `unresolved_reason`). Emission shape left to the implementer. Discovered 2026-04-21 during a descripex surface audit. ([Opus] model-hint marker from the legacy ROADMAP dropped — retired-era convention.)

task.body:
Emit, per WS exchange, the dispatch table CCXT's Pro class uses to route an inbound frame to its parse handler. CCXT routes every WS message through `handleMessage(client, message)` (in `priv/ccxt/ts/src/pro/<id>.ts`), which reads one or more discriminator fields (e.g. `safeString(message, 'channel' | 'topic' | 'e' | 'type' | 'op')`) and dispatches to a `handle<Channel>` method — either through a `methods`/`handlers` object-literal map (channel-string → handler-name) or an if/switch chain that calls the handlers directly. This task extracts that channel → handler mapping plus the discriminator field(s) read, so a consumer knows which parse handler owns a given inbound channel frame. The watch*/subscribe side (channel-name templates) is Task 91; this is the receive/parse side. Source `handle*`/`watch*` ASTs are already on disk in `priv/discoveries/ws_methods.json` — reuse them rather than re-parsing where possible.

Classification is structural, mirroring the shipped Tasks 92 (ws_auth) / 93 (ws_heartbeat): the handler name is the literal identifier invoked, the discriminator is the literal key argument to the `safeString`/`safeValue` lookup. An unrecognized dispatch shape lands in an `unresolved` entry with a reason — never a guessed mapping. Resolve extends-chain inheritance via the WS class hierarchy (a variant/alias Pro class that does not define `handleMessage` inherits its parent's table), exactly as `WsHeartbeat.build/2` walks the `extends` chain. task.body:
Emit, per WS exchange, how the orderbook channel signals a full snapshot vs an incremental delta, and the fields a consumer needs to apply deltas correctly. CCXT's `handleOrderBook(client, message)` (and helpers `handleDelta`/`handleSnapshot`/`handleOrderBookMessage` in `priv/ccxt/ts/src/pro/<id>.ts`) distinguishes a snapshot (full book, local book reset) from a delta (incremental bid/ask changes) via a discriminator — e.g. bybit `type: 'snapshot' | 'delta'`, okx `action: 'snapshot' | 'update'` + a crc32 `checksum`, binance a REST-seeded snapshot followed by `depthUpdate` deltas keyed by first/final update ids (`U`/`u`, plus `pu` on futures). task.title: Audit-surfaced: ws_heartbeat scoped extraction drops extends-chain ancestors
acceptance_criteria: A scoped run naming a variant without its WS root (e.g. --exchange binanceusdm) on a fresh corpus writes the extends-chain ancestors alongside the requested entries
WsHeartbeat.build/2 derives the correct inherited keep_alive_ms / keep_alive_resolved_from for the variant after such a scoped run (no base_default fallback when a parent set keepAlive)
The scoped AggregateWriter merge does not produce duplicate ancestor entries
A unit test covers the ancestor-closure helper directly
mix ccxt_extract.determinism_check byte-identical across two runs; mix ccxt_extract.contract_test passes
task.body:
WsHeartbeat.build/2 resolves keep_alive_ms, ping_kind, and has_pong_handler through the WS-class `extends` chain via the discovery lookup. A scoped extractor run that names a variant without its WS root — e.g. `mix ccxt_extract.ws_heartbeat --exchange binanceusdm` (or `mix ccxt_extract.update --exchange binanceusdm`) against a fresh corpus with no prior ws_heartbeat.json — writes only the child entry. build/2 then cannot find the binance parent in the lookup, treats the chain as ending at the child, falls back to the base client default, and emits keep_alive_ms 30000 with source / keep_alive_resolved_from "base_default" — a silently wrong value AND a dishonest provenance claim (the truth is binance's inherited keepAlive 180000). This violates the project's "every value is provable or explicitly unprovable — no silent guesses" rule.

Tier-flag scoping is unaffected: tier flags expand to whole families via class_hierarchy.json, so --tier1 already pulls binance + binanceusdm together. The trigger is an explicit --exchange naming a child variant without its WS root, on a corpus where the root's ws_heartbeat entry is not already on disk (a fresh worktree before link_corpus, or a fresh --output directory).

Fix direction: close the scoped entry set over its extends-chain ancestors before write. Add a WsHeartbeat ancestor-closure helper that pulls every missing ancestor from the full extract/0 result, and expand the scope MapSet passed to AggregateWriter.write! to include the ancestor ids — without that expansion the scoped merge keeps the stale on-disk ancestor copy AND appends the fresh one, producing duplicate entries.

Corroborated by 3 reasoners in the post-merge audit of commit 4dce59c (Task 93): the Codex GitHub-bot review flagged it P1 on PR #32, the audit-review Codex second-opinion dispatch flagged it P8, and Claude confirmed it.
